caption: A bolt of lightning strikes the ground in a desert, and a puff of dust rises from the spot after the flash.

sa.check: A bolt of lightning strikes the ground.
A puff of dust rises from the strike point after the flash.
The strike point is on open ground, not on a rock or plant.
The bolt and flash come first and the dust follows.

pc.expect: The bolt and flash are brief and gone; the dust appears at the strike point only afterwards and spreads from there; no glow is left on the sand.
pc.fail: The bolt stands as a steady lit line for the rest of the clip; or the dust rises before the bolt arrives; or the dust puff shrinks back into the ground; or the strike point glows like an ember afterwards.

pc.expect: The desert and whatever is in it are the same before and after; the flash reveals what was there and the dust is the only new thing.
pc.fail: Rocks or plants appear or vanish between dark and lit frames; or the dunes change shape; or an object appears at the strike point; or a second dust puff rises where no bolt struck.

pc.expect: The dust rises as a puff, billows upward and spreads, then thins; grains thrown up fall back to the sand.
pc.fail: The dust flows along the ground like water and never rises; or hangs as a fixed shape; or grains rise steadily and stay aloft; or the puff moves as a solid ball.

pc.expect: The bolt is a jagged, branching bright line with a main channel from the sky to the strike point.
pc.fail: The bolt is a perfectly straight beam; or a smooth wave; or a wide glowing tube; or a bolt that hangs in mid-air not reaching the ground while the dust rises.

pc.expect: The ground stays ground: the bolt ends at the surface and does not continue beneath it; the sand does not open.
pc.fail: The bolt continues below the surface as a lit line under the sand; or the ground splits open; or a hole appears that swallows the sand; or the sand becomes transparent.

pc.expect: The sand's colour, the sky and any distant features keep their colours apart from the flash.
pc.fail: The sand changes colour; or the sky turns to daylight after the flash; or distant hills change shape or colour.
